newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Amnesty says Portuguese police mistreat, torture.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says Portuguese police mistreat, torture.

text.p: The most serious violations of human rights in Portugal are cases of physical torture and mistreatment by the police, Amnesty International secretary-general Pierre Sane was quoted as saying on Monday.
"The problems that worry Amnesty International most are torture and mistreatment by the Portuguese police," Sane told Diario Economico newspaper in an interview during a visit to Portugal.

Asked how the problem could be solved, he said: "The priorities are to change the behaviour of members of the security forces and put an end to the climate of impunity by introducing reforms to improve the criminal justice system."
He said additional financing should be allocated to help modernise the police force, improve training of recruits and the quality of life in jails.
Sane said the authorities must open investigations into every case or torture and mistreatment in order to punish those responsible through the justice system.
Last month the European Committee against Torture accused Portuguese police of frequently mistreating people in their custody, saying the most common abuse was blows inflicted with fists or clubs.

The committee, an expert body charged with ensuring respect for the European Convention to Prevent Torture and Inhuman or Degrading Treatments, levelled the accusations in a report following a visit to Portugal from May 14-26, 1995.
The report contained a reply from the Portuguese government saying it was worried about the phenomenon of police brutality but that it was less widespread than alleged in the report.
